## Summary

- dual-write immutable action receipts for review batches/items/retries, review logs/comments, apply actions/batches, and publication phases
- finalize and publish validated shard state on success, partial, interrupted, timeout, blocked, skipped, and failure paths without changing legacy behavior
- wire workflow proof artifacts and publication jobs, with focused identity, parent/phase, idempotency, failure-path, and workflow tests

## Stack

Depends on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/511

## Validation

- `node --test test/*.test.ts` (977 passed)
- `node --test test/repair/*.test.ts dist/repair/*.test.js` (723 passed)
- changed coverage: 100% lines, 88.61% branches, 100% functions
- full coverage: 74.78% lines, 71.68% branches, 83.79% functions
- direct TypeScript builds, all ESLint lanes, oxfmt check, active-surface/limit checks, YAML parse, and `git diff --check`

`pnpm run check` was not invoked verbatim because pnpm attempted to replace the shared symlinked `node_modules` in this worktree; its component checks were run directly on Node 26.5.0.

target.title: fix(tavily): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the Tavily web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — Tavily is one of the web search providers that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. The web search runtime threads `signal` into `execute(args, { signal })`, but the Tavily provider ignored it — so aborted runs left Tavily requests open until their configured timeout.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted Tavily request caught by `runWebSearch`'s catch block can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Tavily signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the Tavily provider and client to `postTrustedWebToolsJson` (which already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141). The pattern matches the searxng fix in #104216 and the DuckDuckGo fix in #104899 — one provider per PR, no new SDK surface.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path Tavily uses:
- Production: `postTrustedWebToolsJson({ signal })` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`
- Proof: `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` — same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()` code path; only the SSRF policy differs (selfHosted allows localhost for proof).

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 122ms through guarded-fetch stack
        (withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:44061/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

Proof script: `extensions/tavily/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

### Signal chain — full path (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| Tavily provider tool | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts` | 28 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| Tavily POST helper | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts` | 90 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted POST endpoint | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 150 | `signal: params.signal` — native support |

No new SDK surface is needed — `postTrustedWebToolsJson` already accepts `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tavily/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ tavily tools: 15/15 passed (including signal forwarding test)
 ✓ tavily client: 5/5 passed
 ✓ runtime: 31/31 passed (including "does not fall back after parent cancellation")
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-tools.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### Landing order

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) and #104899 (DuckDuckGo, same author) also add the same guard. Whichever lands first, the others will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: feat(ledger): add immutable action history core
target.body:
## Summary

- add immutable, create-only JSONL action shards with deterministic replay and conflict detection
- restrict identity inputs to strict canonical JSON with safe integers only; large identifiers must be strings
- require explicit outcome-independent idempotency identities for mutations
- bind repository and SHA into replay-stable producer identities and shard paths
- preserve source timestamps while deterministically sorting causal children after parents
- keep CrabFleet projection failures durable without logging response bodies

## Independent Review Hardening

- snapshot every parent directory by device and inode immediately around open, write, hard-link, and cleanup mutations
- verify opened descriptors and linked files still identify the expected path; parent swaps fail closed before reporting success
- reject whitespace-delimited and mixed-case bearer/API credentials plus case-insensitive private paths
- reject credential identity aliases including `authToken`, `githubToken`, `refresh_token`, and `cloudflareApiToken`
- reject unsafe JavaScript integers before identity hashing
- align schema and runtime rejection for private IPv6, dot-only paths, UNC/backslash paths, mixed-case private paths, credential-bearing paths, and unsafe integers

## Design

- local writers spool one immutable event file per transition
- workflow finalization batches events into one digest-addressed shard per full producer identity
- shard paths are `ledger/v1/events/YYYY/MM/DD/<producer-repo>/<producer>/<run-attempt-job-digest>.jsonl`
- shard partitions derive only from immutable workflow metadata or an explicit stable date
- source timestamps remain evidence; causal topology resolves ordering conflicts
- mutable comments, dashboards, sessions, command ledgers, and evidence graphs remain projections

target.body:
## Summary

- split crawl-remote production deployment into an unprivileged preflight runner and a fresh protected deployment runner
- require the selected SHA to equal the current `openclaw/crawl-remote` `main` tip during preflight, before D1 mutation, and again after migrations immediately before Worker deployment
- build and test the exact target SHA without production credentials, then upload only a prebuilt single-file Worker bundle, sanitized Wrangler config, D1 migrations, and a canonical SHA-256 manifest
- fail closed unless Wrangler dry-run emits exactly one regular deployable file named `index.js`
- bind artifact and receipt identity to run ID, run attempt, target SHA, and validated `observation_order_state` (`dormant` or `active`), and retain the artifact for 31 days so it survives the protected-environment approval window
- run the protected job with exact Node `24.18.0` and committed lockfile-backed Wrangler `4.107.1`; it checks out only the trusted ClawSweeper toolchain at `${{ github.sha }}` and never checks out or executes crawl-remote code
- prove the selected D1 fence state before and after migrations, deploy the prebuilt bundle with the exact release SHA, and poll both workers.dev and `reports.openclaw.ai/crawl-remote` until their health and contract endpoints advertise the exact release and selected capability state

## Final reviewer fixes

- run `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` from inside `.github/deploy/crawl-remote-toolchain`; the focused test executes the extracted workflow install against a copied lockfile-backed toolchain
- split D1 mutation and Worker deployment into separate credentialed steps, with a token-only exact-current-main reauthorization directly between them
- parse Wrangler `4.107.1`'s structured D1 `APIError` JSON: exact request path, `name`, `kind`, code `7500`, account tag, and a single exact missing-table diagnostic in `notes`; unrelated failures, extra fields, stderr, and active missing-table bootstrap fail closed
- reject extra Wrangler output modules, nested assets, symlinks, directories, and any bundle layout other than a sole regular `index.js`
- validate release identity and the complete contract independently through both the workers.dev origin and configured production route
- retain the release artifact for 31 days, covering GitHub's 30-day environment approval wait with a one-day margin

## Security boundary

- preflight has no GitHub environment or Cloudflare credential and mints only an exact-repository `Contents: read` App token for `openclaw/crawl-remote`
- deploy runs under `crawl-remote-production` on a fresh runner with `contents: read`, `bash --noprofile --norc`, cleared shell startup channels, and no target lifecycle/test execution
- deploy sparsely checks out only `.github/deploy/crawl-remote-toolchain` from `openclaw/clawsweeper` at `${{ github.sha }}`, with persisted credentials disabled
- only the locked toolchain Wrangler binary may query or mutate Cloudflare resources
- the only Cloudflare secret reference is the environment-specific `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; there is no repository-secret fallback
- an existing `remote_capability_fences` row must exactly match the selected dormant/active state before migrations; a pinned-shape missing-table API error is accepted only for dormant bootstrap
- the verified artifact is bounded by an exact file allowlist and hashes, and its receipt is consumed once before the first mutation
- workflow reruns remain forbidden; a fresh retry must package and deploy the then-current crawl-remote `main`

- exact validated branch head: `bd2a58a829e5b19bffd6c9199afa2dc7fe9cf005`
- focused deployment/action tests: 19/19
- executable adversarial coverage for unsupported Wrangler output modules/assets, cross-origin stale release identity and malformed contracts, real locked toolchain installation, non-current SHA authorization, `main` advancing after D1 migrations, artifact tampering/extras/cross-state reuse, target-controlled execution, realistic Wrangler missing-table `APIError`, unrelated API failures, and strict post-migration fence state
- extracted workflow install with Node `24.18.0` and npm `11.16.0`: Wrangler `4.107.1` installed and verified
- ShellCheck on every workflow `run` block
- `PATH=/private/tmp/clawsweeper-corepack/node_modules/.bin:$PATH pnpm run check`
- crawl-remote merged `main` `d6bb9b7a9c7eff0704dab4845a00e1863b7b8ef1` with Node `24.18.0` and npm `11.16.0`: install, typecheck, 73 tests, Wrangler `4.107.1`, and deployment dry-run
- formatting and `git diff --check`

1. Dispatch must use the current exact `openclaw/crawl-remote` `main` tip; it is currently `d6bb9b7a9c7eff0704dab4845a00e1863b7b8ef1`.
2. The `crawl-remote-production` environment was verified on July 12, 2026 with administrator bypass disabled, required `openclaw/maintainer` approval, self-review prevention enabled, and a custom deployment branch policy allowing only ClawSweeper `main`.
3. `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is still absent from the environment. No rollout was attempted. Before the first deployment, bootstrap it only as an environment secret; do not create a repository fallback.
4. Restrict that custom Cloudflare token to account `91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca` and zone `openclaw.ai`: Account Settings Read, Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, D1 Edit, Workers Routes Edit for the zone, User Details Read, and Memberships Read.
